A: Axial spine CT scan showing focal vertebral osteolytic lesions, a documented radiological manifestation of systemic mastocytosis as described in the figure caption and article text. B: Axial spine CT scan showing mixed focal osteolytic and osteocondensation lesions in the same vertebra, a common mixed radiological pattern of systemic mastocytosis per the article text. C: Sagittal spine MRI (T1 and T2 weighted sequences) showing diffuse bone marrow infiltration with characteristic signal changes consistent with systemic mastocytosis bone involvement as described in the article. D: Spine and pelvis CT scan showing disseminated punctiform osteocondensations, a focal sclerotic bone manifestation of systemic mastocytosis as noted in the figure caption. E: Spine CT scan showing diffuse bone marrow osteosclerosis, a documented radiological feature of systemic mastocytosis per the figure caption.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a Giemsa-stained bone marrow histology image from a patient with systemic mastocytosis, demonstrating perivascular spindle-shaped atypical mast cells with hypogranularity and dense mast cell aggregates, which are specific histologic diagnostic features of systemic mastocytosis. B: Panel B is a CD117 immunohistochemistry-stained bone marrow section from a systemic mastocytosis patient, showing dense mast cell aggregates that confirm the presence of mast cell infiltrates characteristic of the disease. C: Panel C is a CD25 immunohistochemistry-stained bone marrow section from a systemic mastocytosis patient, showing dense mast cell aggregates with membrane reactivity, consistent with the atypical immunophenotype of mast cells in systemic mastocytosis.

in_text_mentions: A follow-up bone marrow biopsy conducted a year later unveiled a myeloid neoplasm with grade 3 myelofibrosis. Notably, atypical mast cell aggregates (Figure 1) were observed, which were positive for CD117 (Figure 2), CD25 (Figure 3), and CD2 (partially, weakly). Molecular analysis confirmed the presence of a KITD816V mutation while elevated serum tryptase levels reached 117 μg/L (Normal 0-11.4). Collectively, these findings were consistent with a diagnosis of systemic mastocytosis with an associated hematological neoplasm.
